messages:
bob_customer: Hey, hitting a weird one — our on-prem service (VPC-peered) suddenly started routing Redwood API calls through eu-west and we're seeing ~250ms p95 and some 403s. Verified the app is configured to call us-west. Any ideas? :thinking:

alice_support: Sorry you're seeing this, Bob. Can you paste a minimal curl + the public IP you see from the server? Also the VPC/peering details if possible.

bob_customer: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/generate
* Connected to api.redwood.com (18.203.45.22) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/chat/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.com
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< x-region: eu-west-1
< x-request-id: r-abc123

From the host, `curl ifconfig.me` shows 3.248.56.12 which geo-locates to Ireland (we're in us-west).

chloe_infra: That x-region header is interesting — it means our edge saw the request as EU. Two common causes for this with peered/on-prem setups: 1) egress hairpin through a hub NAT in EU region (SNAT applied there) 2) a transparent proxy/load-balancer in the peering path re-issuing the request from an EU egress IP.

alice_support: Can you run these quick checks and paste results?
```
# from your app host
ip route get 8.8.8.8
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.com:443:18.203.45.22 https://api.redwood.com/v1/health
traceroute -n api.redwood.com
sudo tcpdump -n -s 0 -c 200 host api.redwood.com and tcp port 443 -w /tmp/api-egress.pcap
```

bob_customer: Running now, attaching snippets:
```
$ ip route get 8.8.8.8
8.8.8.8 via 10.10.0.1 dev eth0 src 10.10.1.32 uid 1000
    cache
$ traceroute -n api.redwood.com
 1  10.10.0.1  0.3 ms  0.2 ms  0.3 ms
 2  100.64.0.5  1.1 ms  1.0 ms  1.2 ms
 3  52.16.0.10  8.0 ms  7.8 ms  8.1 ms
 4  3.250.14.40 (3.250.14.40)  42.1 ms  41.9 ms  41.8 ms
```

pcap: I've uploaded `/tmp/api-egress.pcap` to our S3 share (link provided privately).

chloe_infra: Thanks — traceroute hop 4 IP 3.250.14.40 is an AWS EU egress IP (matches eu-west NAT). That suggests your VPC peering is routing 0.0.0.0/0 toward a transit hub in EU which performs SNAT. Do you have a transit VPC or hub that centralizes internet egress?

bob_customer: Yes, we have a peered transit hub in eu-west for some legacy services. We thought only specific prefixes would be routed there. Route tables show a 0.0.0.0/0 target to the transit attachment in the hub for one of our subnets — looks like a regressive change.

sam_sre: Quick mitigation while we debug: add a subnet route override for the app subnet to point 0.0.0.0/0 to your local NAT gateway in us-west (or a direct IGW) so it egresses from the correct region. Also check the peering/propagation rules in the hub — some route-propagation updates can leak default routes.

alice_support: For the 403s: when API keys are used from an unexpected region we apply stricter auth checks (tenant policy + geofencing) which can produce 403s and also route to regional enforcement proxies. That could explain both errors and the x-region header. We'll flag this as an escalation to infra so they can check transit peering policies and route propagation.

bob_customer: Will try the subnet override. One Q — will changing egress to our us NAT cause a billing delta? We got billed as EU for some calls this week and need to reconcile.

chloe_infra: Yes, egress/billing is tied to the egress IP/region. If your traffic egressed from eu-west, that's where the request counted. Fixing the route will stop future mis-billing but we'll need to reconcile historical invoices (support can open a billing ticket).

sam_sre: Action items: 1) Bob add the temporary route override and confirm curl/resolution results 2) Bob share the pcap link and VPC IDs (we already have the traceroute) 3) Infra (Chloe) to check transit hub route-propagation ACLs + any recent IaC changes (Terraform plans) that may have pushed a default route into the peering table 4) Support to open a billing case for EU-ingress charges and record timestamps.

bob_customer: Done — I added the route override and retested:
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED"
* Connected to api.redwood.com (18.203.45.22) port 443 (#0)
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< x-region: us-west-2
< x-request-id: r-abc456
```

Latency back to normal and 200s now. Thanks! :tada:

alice_support: Great. I'll keep this thread open while Chloe audits the hub and Sam files the billing ticket. Chloe — any idea on likely root cause?

chloe_infra: Preliminary: a bad Terraform apply last night (a propagated default route got enabled for one of the spoke attachments). That allowed the spoke subnets to prefer the hub for internet egress; the hub SNAT'd to EU NAT. Root cause = route-propagation + missing per-spoke override in Terraform module. I'll prepare a PR to revert the propagation and add explicit egress route rules.

sam_sre: Billing ticket opened (case #BI-4237) with timestamps for the window where traceroute showed eu egress. I'll follow up.

bob_customer: Appreciate the quick help. Please leave any suggested guardrails — we'd like to prevent this from happening again.

chloe_infra: Suggested guardrails: 1) add a per-spoke explicit 0.0.0.0/0 preference for local NAT in Terraform modules 2) disallow default-route propagation in hub unless opt-in 3) add egress sanity tests in CI that run from a test spoke and assert geolocation of ifconfig.me == expected region IP. We can share example terraform snippet if helpful.

alice_support: Thanks everyone. Bob — if anything reappears, ping this thread and we'll reopen. Closing after infra confirms PR and billing reconciliation. :white_check_mark:
